system_overview: This specification models a trivially simple algorithm that repeatedly increments a counter by two, starting from zero. Its primary purpose is educational: it serves as a beginner exercise for learning formal proof techniques in the TLA+ proof system. The specification includes machine-checked proofs that the counter remains a natural number and that it is always divisible by two.
actors_and_components: The system consists of a single sequential process that executes an infinite loop. There are no concurrent actors or distributed components.
state_variables: The system tracks a single integer counter representing the accumulated value after successive additions of two.
actions: There is exactly one action: the counter is incremented by two. This action repeats indefinitely in an infinite loop.
safety_properties: Type correctness: the counter is always a natural number (non-negative integer). Evenness: the counter is always evenly divisible by two -- that is, there always exists a natural number that, when multiplied by two, equals the counter value.
additional_assumptions: The specification is written using PlusCal syntax which is translated to TLA+. The specification includes formal proofs of both the type invariant and the evenness property, structured as hierarchical proof steps with base case, stuttering case, and inductive case.
